description:
About the Position

KTH’s Department of Applied Physics is recruiting a postdoctoral researcher in sustainable materials and electrochemical processes. Applications include water treatment, resource recovery and renewable chemical production.

Research Position Overview

Develop nanomaterials and reactor concepts, investigate interfaces and catalytic mechanisms, and use characterisation and data-assisted optimisation to evaluate performance.

Research Areas

  • Electrochemical systems
  • Water treatment and resource recovery
  • Sustainable nanomaterials

Funding and Duration

Employment and financial support
ComponentDetails
PositionPostdoctoral employee
SalaryMonthly salary; amount not published in the advert.
DurationUp to two years; full-time temporary employment.
BenefitsEmployment benefits follow KTH’s applicable terms; no numerical salary is stated.
Programme / host supportSalaried KTH postdoctoral employment.

Eligibility and Requirements

Academic preparation and skills
ComponentDetails
Applicant eligibilityWorldwide, subject to the official qualifications and recruitment checks.
Academic preparationRelevant doctorate completed by the employment decision.
Research skillsDocumented publications and materials research in electrochemistry, environmental technologies or renewable energy.
LanguageExcellent spoken and written English required.

Application dates

Recruitment dates and location
ComponentDetails
Recruitment statusOpen when checked on 15 October 2026
Deadline16 October 2026, midnight Stockholm time (CEST).
Start dateBy agreement.
LocationStockholm, Sweden

How to Apply

  • CV, diplomas and grades, with English/Swedish translations where needed.
  • Research-interest and motivation account: maximum two pages.

Submit through the application button on the official recruitment page.

Selection and Contact

A doctorate awarded within the previous three years is preferred, rather than listed as an absolute requirement.

Project contact: Professor Joydeep Dutta.

About KTH Royal Institute of Technology

The host is the Department of Applied Physics in KTH’s School of Engineering Sciences, Stockholm. The role includes research collaboration and student supervision.
